quick.summary: How to cool down an argument and get back to solving the problem.
quick.takeaway: Hear them out. Repeat their worry back to them before you answer.

parts.title: Hear them out

beats.line: I gave my reason for the layout. The product manager just got louder. Why?
Think of a tea stall. You order tea, and the seller just stares.
I would say my order again, but louder.
Exactly. They want to know they were heard. This requires empathetic active listening.
Can I just say hear them out?
Yes. Hear them out. Repeat their worry back to them before you answer.
I hear you are worried about the deadline. Like that?
Yes. Once they know you hear them, they will quiet down.
What if they are loud because my idea is just bad?

parts.cliff: How to handle a truly bad idea.

beats.line: If your idea misses the mark, do not defend it. Shift to learning.
So I just give up and agree with them?
No. Think of a detective. They do not argue, they ask for clues.
How does a designer ask for clues?
Ask what evidence they have. Ask what success looks like to them.
So I ask, what metric are we trying to move here?
Yes. You stop fighting and start looking at the facts together.
Then we solve the real problem, not my broken idea.
Exactly. Curiosity beats defending a bad design every time.

quiz.question: When someone gets loud and argumentative, what do they usually want?
options: They want to know they were heard.
They want you to speak louder.
They want to cancel the project.
quiz.explanation: People repeat themselves louder when they feel ignored. Repeating their worry back solves this.

quiz.question: If you realize your idea is bad, you should defend it anyway.
quiz.explanation: Never defend a broken idea. Shift into detective mode and ask questions to learn the real problem.
